questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

It is an ______ day to start your new business.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. auspicious**

The sentence refers to the beginning of a new business, this should ideally begin on a good occasion. Option 1 'occasional' refers to **something that happens once in a while and thus cannot be a day to start a business**. Option 2 is incorrect because and **an 'ominous' day is a bad day to start a business**. 'Audacious' refers **to a person that is bold and cannot be applied to a day. So we left with auspicious which means showing or suggesting that future success is likely: PROPITIOUS**

**Thus, the correct answer is option 3. **

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The modern man is busy acquiring more and more wealth and designing ways to invest it in more sense pleasures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option "2"**

 
• The original sentence refers to the modern man acquiring more wealth in order to invest in pleasures, thus the term 'pleasures' acting as a noun should have an adjective before that describes it. This would be the adjective form of the verb 'sense', thus it would be 'sensory'.
 
• Correct Sentence :- The modern man is busy acquiring more and more wealth and designing ways to invest it in more **sensory** pleasures.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said to me, "What are you doing?"

options.text: He asked me what I was doing.
He asked me that what was I doing.
He said that what I was doing
He said what I had been doing.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. He asked me what I was doing.**

__
 
• We make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the reported speech is an interrogative sentence we follow these steps-
 
 
• Reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'asked'.
 
• Change the sentence, given in the reported speech__, from interrogative to assertive.
 
• Tense of reported speech is changed accordingly. ( in above sentence- 'are' changes into 'was')
 
• personal Pronouns of reported speech are changed as per subject and object of reporting verb. Here, the second person- 'You' will change into 'I' as per object - 'me' (hidden).
 
 
 
• By following these steps we get the final sentence - *" He asked me what I was doing**."*

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Nevertheless, sound health, economic security and mental satisfaction are desired by all

B. A change that is conducive to happiness may be termed as progress.

C. But different people find happiness in different things.

D. So, If a change contributes to the growth of these factors, it is progress.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. BCAD**

The passage starts with an introduction to the topic at hand with **statement B**, this talks about how a change that causes happiness is called progress, then comes **statement C** which talks about how happiness is subjective. Then comes **statement A** which talks about some common contributors to happiness and finally there comes **statement D** which talks about how the change contributes to these factors.

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

C. I am going to jungle safari tomorrow.

D. My friend told me that jungle is beautiful in these days.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. CDAB**

The passage begins with an introduction to the topic at hand in **statement C** - the narrator going to a jungle safari, the next **statement - D **- involves the narrator describing the jungle. This is followed by **statement A**, this talks about the narrator asking his friend to borrow his camera and the final statement - **statement B** - talks about the narrator promising to return the camera the following week. 

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:

The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for America.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. have left**

As a rule, when a sentence refers to 2 subjects, the **verbs in the sentence should refer to the subject that comes first**. Here it is 'the Prime Minister' and he is a singular entity, thus the verbs should also be singular. Thus, **'have' needs to be replaced with 'has'.**

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined segment of the given sentence. If no substitution is required select ‘No improvement’**

A man in need __pleaded for help.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'No improvement'.**

__
 
• The sentence **does not have any errors** and thus needs no improvement.
 
• '**P******lea **for help' **means **'an urgent and emotional request'**
 
 
• ***Example:** He made a **plea for help**/mercy.*
 
 
 
• *​*The preposition '**in**' takes a noun or a pronoun. In the given sentence '**need**' is a noun. '**Pleaded'** is a verb here and it is an intransitive verb.

Hence ***option 2*** is the most appropriate answer here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

The thief was being arrested by the police.

options.text: The police were arresting the thief.
The police had arrested the thief.
The police has arrested the thief.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. The police were arresting the thief**

The original sentence is in the passive voice, the format for this is 

**Object + was + being + Past tense of verb + by + Subject**

This needs to be converted to the active voice, the format for that will be

**Subject + was + Past continuous of the Verb + Object**

The police were arresting the thief

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

The correct answer is** option 3 i.e. on foot**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **One's legs **is used as a means of transport.
 
• The idiom **'on shank's mare'** refers to the act of walking on one's own feet to reach one's destination.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/028581a18ec4485d81de787082ee6b57d08426b1eff9da39c1249541d0b62dd6.png] Note:__ ***Shanks' mare (or nag or pony) derives from the name of the lower part of the leg between the knee and ankle - the shank, nowadays more often known as the shin-bone or tibia. This was alluded to in the early form of this term - shank's nag. This originated in Scotland in the 18th century. There are several early citations in Scottish literature, as herein Robert Fergusson's Poems on Various Subjects, 1774.*

Thus, the correct answer is** option 3.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

He ______ a heinous crime.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2 i.e. committed**

The sentence refers to a crime, and crime doesn't just 'happen', it is not something that can be 'made' and it is not something that 'occurs' on its own. A crime is 'committed' by a person. 

**Thus, the correct answer is option 2. **
